The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' stored spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Why, in plain words: After a feature setting was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored running total for the month, so those stored totals fell behind what shoppers had actually bought.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 6d 23h 59m 56s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken - recommends: revert monthly-spend-feature
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #572 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' stored spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Incident: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
Date: Nov 05, 2026, 13:02 UTC, not back to normal by Nov 12, 2026, 13:01:56 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 9 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 13:07:22 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 13:01:40 UTC
Ended by: Argus: recommended to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 13:01:56 UTC - revert monthly-spend-feature

Summary
The service broke at Nov 05, 13:02 UTC and was not back to normal by Nov 12, 13:01:56 UTC, at least 6 days 23 hours 59 minutes 56 seconds later. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. After a feature setting was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored running total for the month, so those stored totals fell behind what shoppers had actually bought. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #572, for a person to review and merge. Argus recommends this and did not take it: revert monthly-spend-feature. While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, shoppers' stored month totals could keep falling further behind with every purchase, the totals already short stay wrong until someone rewrites them, and the monthly statements and per-item spend averages that read those totals could show shoppers the wrong figures.

Impact
at least 6d 23h 59m 56s - since onset, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-05T13:02:00Z. Found by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 days, so the fault is up to that old.

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, `record_a_purchase` in `src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py` records each purchase through `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which adds the purchase to `purchases` and moves `total_cents` but never writes `total_this_month_cents`. Each shopper's stored month total therefore stays where it was while their this-month purchases grow, and falls further below their sum with every purchase. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom The stored spend totals of the shoppers checked no longer matched the purchases behind them, falling short of what had been bought, starting from purchases recorded at the onset.
  Evidence:
    AL1
why 1 A shopper's stored month total did not grow as their purchases were recorded, so it fell below the sum of their this-month purchase prices, which is what the reconciliation compares it with.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    U4 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
    U5 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:115, in _the_disagreement_in: subtracts with it: _bought_this_month(account) - account.total_this_month_cents, where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
why 2 Purchases began going through a different recording path when admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at 13:01:35 UTC, shortly before the oldest affected purchase. No deploy came back for the window searched. No earlier change was ruled out: no metrics from before the onset were read, and nothing else in the record shows the service healthy with an earlier change in place.
  Evidence:
    P1 13:01:35 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    T13 Nov 12 13:01:55 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 05 13:03
    AL1
why 3 With the flag on, purchases are recorded through a path that, by Code-Fix's reading, does not update the stored month total.
  Evidence:
    F1
Contributing factors
- The spend-integrity check that found the fault runs only every 7 days, and no other check comparing stored month totals with purchases was seen. (AI-3)
- Before monthly-spend-feature was switched on, no test or check was seen confirming that the flag-on purchase path keeps the stored month total in line with the purchases. By Code-Fix's account, the derive-path cases it adds would fail against the old code. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 13:01:35 UTC. From the first affected purchase at 13:02 UTC, the stored shopper spend totals were written wrong. All 240 checked totals now disagree with their purchases, and the widest is short by 1,297.31. Serving was unaffected: errors, latency and traffic stayed at baseline. | 0.60 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken
C2 | Switching on the flag monthly-spend-feature at 13:01:35 UTC changed how spend totals are computed, so totals no longer match the purchases. Unlike the first explanation, this one assumes no wrong stored values were left behind. | 0.35 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 13:01:35 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | Nov 12 13:01:56 | Refused to act on C1 - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | Nov 12 13:04:48 | Proposed a fix: PR #572 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 13:02 UTC. SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile fired at Nov 12, 2026, 13:01:40 UTC, 6 days 23 hours 59 minutes 40 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #572 | open
AI-2 | Revert monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Run the monthly-total reconciliation (`reconcile_monthly_totals`) on a much shorter schedule than the current spend-integrity check, so short totals are found soon after they start. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Before any feature flag that switches how purchases are recorded is turned on in production, require tests that record purchases through both the flag-on and flag-off paths and confirm the stored totals reconcile with the purchases. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Link the SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert to an on-call paging policy so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Once the flag is reverted or the fix is merged, run `src/io_shop/repair_monthly_totals.py` as a dry run, review the accounts it plans to fix, then run it with `apply=True`, supplying a loader and saver for production storage. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Look into the accounts the repair script lists as having month totals above their purchases, which it leaves unchanged. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | If the repair runs after November has ended, check and correct the November month totals separately, since the script covers only the current month. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-9 | Find out whether any monthly statements or spend averages shown to shoppers since the onset were built from short month totals, and decide whether to correct them for those shoppers. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
Argus declined to act, and recommends: revert monthly-spend-feature

Lessons learned
What went well
- 3 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at Nov 05 13:02.
- 15 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 05 13:03.
- 16 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus left for a person to do - reverting monthly-spend-feature for C1.
- 3 minutes 8 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #572.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so the recommended revert and the repair waited on someone noticing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/4bb91b87-642a-49a6-a5b0-2afc02a54217
The fix it proposed: PR #572 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/572) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 13:01:35 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Read; none came back.
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py has two ways to record a purchase, and record_a_purchase picks one using the rollout decision passed to it. With the decision on, it calls record_purchase_deriving_the_month. That function added the purchase to purchases and moved total_cents, but did not write total_this_month_cents at all. Each purchase a shopper made this month went into their history while their stored month total stayed where it was, so the total fell further behind with every purchase. That fits the investigation's evidence: every checked shopper total disagrees with its purchases, the totals are short, and the oldest bad record comes 25 seconds after monthly-spend-feature was switched on. It also fits the lack of errors, because a total that is simply too low raises nothing.

The fix, in src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py: record_purchase_deriving_the_month now writes total_this_month_cents as the sum of price_cents over the account's purchases flagged in_current_month, new purchase included. Because the figure is worked out from the history, an account that was already short is set right by its next purchase on this path. The flag-off path, record_purchase, is unchanged. record_a_purchase and its signature are unchanged. The flag can be turned back on with both paths writing a month total that matches the purchases.

Tests: tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py keeps every existing test and adds cases for the derive path. They check that it moves the month total, leaves it alone for an earlier month's purchase, still moves the lifetime total, and corrects a total that arrived short. One more case records several purchases through record_a_purchase with the flag on and off, then checks that the stored month total equals the sum of the prices and that reconcile_monthly_totals finds no disagreement. Against the old code, the derive-path cases would fail because the month total stays where it was. None of these tests, nor the fix, has been run.

Repair: src/io_shop/repair_monthly_totals.py is a one-off script. It has not been run, and a person has to run it. It only fixes totals that are short: the stored total_this_month_cents is below the sum of the account's this-month purchases. For those accounts it rewrites the stored figure to that sum. Totals that are too high would point to a different fault, so it leaves them unchanged and lists them for someone to look at. It reads accounts from a loader and writes through a saver that whoever runs it supplies, because there is no storage layer in this repository for it to use. It does a dry run by default and writes only when called with apply=True. It also only covers the current month, because a purchase carries a this-month flag rather than a date. If the month has turned over since 2026-11-05, someone has to check the November totals separately. tests/io_shop/test_repair_monthly_totals.py covers which accounts it plans to fix, which it leaves alone, and that a dry run writes nothing.
How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main
U1 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:650, in the_mean_purchase_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
U2 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:882, in _compared_with_usual: reads it: this_month_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
U3 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:918, in render_monthly_statement: reads it: month_total_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
U4 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
U5 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:115, in _the_disagreement_in: subtracts with it: _bought_this_month(account) - account.total_this_month_cents, where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
U6 | total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, the stored monthly spend totals for shoppers who made purchases after a feature setting was switched on fell short of what those shoppers had actually bought. The likely cause is that once the setting was on, the shop recorded each purchase but did not add it to the shopper's stored running total for the month. The problem lasted {duration}. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in lost takings at {customer_loss}. No one was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus did not act on the suspected cause itself. Nothing could show whether the step that would test it worked within the time Argus waits, so Argus recommends reverting the monthly-spend-feature setting rather than doing it. Argus has also proposed a fix, which is open as a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
